mission: Find movies and series that create a strong need to understand an impossible situation, phenomenon, organism, experiment, system, or reality-bending rule set. Discovery and concept escalation matter more than raw action.

strong_positive_signals.signal: Scientists actively investigating an unexplained or impossible phenomenon
Biology, genetics, mutation, alien organisms, ecology, parasites, evolution or unusual physiology
Unknown phenomenon whose rules are discovered through observation, testing or deduction
High-concept premise that keeps revealing new implications instead of stopping at one gimmick
Scientific experiments or technologies with unexpected consequences
Reality distortion, time anomalies, memory anomalies or consciousness manipulation
Artificial systems, games, facilities or social experiments whose hidden rules/purpose must be discovered
Suspense driven by needing to know what is actually happening
Conspiracies or secret research programs connected to the central phenomenon

negative_signals.signal: Straightforward monster/creature escape after the threat is revealed
Generic slasher, torture or psychological horror where the science/mystery is secondary
Space opera, franchise lore, military spectacle or action-first sci-fi with little investigation
Slow pacing where the movie withholds information without providing meaningful discoveries
Sequel or remake that mostly repeats an already-seen concept without a substantial new idea
Mystery whose payoff is primarily symbolic/ambiguous and not supported by ongoing discoveries

reference_titles.title: Fringe
reference_titles.why: Ideal reference: scientific investigation, bizarre cases, biology, experiments, conspiracies and escalating mythology.

reference_titles.title: Arrival
reference_titles.why: Scientists/language experts seriously investigate an alien phenomenon; patient pacing is fine because discoveries keep mattering.

reference_titles.title: Annihilation
reference_titles.why: Scientists enter an unknown zone full of continuously evolving biological impossibilities.

reference_titles.title: Lucy
reference_titles.why: A scientific premise keeps escalating into larger and stranger implications.

reference_titles.title: The Platform
reference_titles.why: Bizarre artificial system with unknown rules, purpose and social consequences.

reference_titles.title: Circle
reference_titles.why: Immediate high-concept situation where people theorize, test and exploit unknown rules.

reference_titles.title: Cube
reference_titles.why: Hidden system, mathematical clues and survival through understanding the structure.

reference_titles.title: Cube 2: Hypercube
reference_titles.why: Extends the rule-discovery premise into stranger physics and dimensions.

reference_titles.title: Spectral
reference_titles.why: Interesting phenomenon, but became too military/action-focused.

reference_titles.title: Weapons
reference_titles.why: Strange premise, but the investigation felt too withholding/boring.

reference_titles.title: Underwater
reference_titles.why: Interesting setup but too much straightforward escape-the-monsters/catastrophe.

reference_titles.title: Saw
reference_titles.why: Leans too heavily toward psychological horror/torture rather than scientific mystery.

reference_titles.title: The Platform 2
reference_titles.why: Too repetitive; did not introduce enough fresh conceptual territory.
